title: Face & neck booking page: choose the structure
question: Same L'amour De Soi look in all three (light bone ground, dark ink text, one deep pine for actions, the stencil wordmark). What changes is how the page leads a visitor from the ad to a booked hour. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The room on Rosslyn Hill
options.lineage: Place-led: the real clinic opens the page
options.thesis: Open on the actual Hampstead clinic, then hand her the appointment: place, price and hour in one glance.
options.viewport: Phone: wordmark bar; a short band of the real Rosslyn Hill interior with the address on it; headline; '£149 · 1 hour · paid at the clinic'; one pine button. Desktop: copy left, photo full height right.
options.risk: The best real photo is the reception and retail floor, not a treatment room, so it sells the place more than the treatment.

options.label: The appointment book
options.lineage: Booking-led: the calendar is the hero
options.thesis: The calendar is the hero: price, place and the next open days are on screen together, so the first tap is a date.
options.viewport: Phone: wordmark bar; short headline; price row; the next open days as a strip already visible above the fold; tapping a day opens the hours in place. Desktop: offer left, booking card pinned right.
options.risk: Asks for a date before any proof; the short clinic proof and 'what you're booking' have to squeeze into the hero column.

options.label: The hour
options.lineage: Visit-led: the hour you are booking is the spine
options.thesis: Sell the hour itself: one ribbon runs down the page from arrival to aftercare and ends in the booking.
options.viewport: Phone: headline, '£149 · 1 hour · paid at the clinic', pine button; the ribbon starts at the fold with 'Arrive at 40 Rosslyn Hill' as its first mark.
options.risk: Only the phases are confirmed, not the minutes inside the hour, so the ribbon marks stages and never times.
